rows: Zions Bancorporation, N.A. One South Main Salt Lake City, UT 84133 October 19, 2026 |
Zions Bancorporation, N.A. reports 3Q26 net earnings of $262 million and diluted EPS of $1.78
compared with 3Q25 net earnings of $221 million and diluted EPS of $1.48, and 2Q26 net earnings of $452 million and diluted EPS of $3.05
Net earnings per diluted common share |  | Net earnings |  | Return on average tangible common equity 2 |  | Estimated common equity tier 1 ratio
Net Interest Income and NIM | • | Net interest income was $684 million, up 2%
Operating Performance | • | Pre-provision net revenue² ("PPNR") was $340 million, down 1%
• | Customer-related noninterest income was $192 million, up 18%; adjusted customer-related noninterest income 2 was $182 million, up 5%
• | Noninterest expense was $553 million, up 5%; adjusted noninterest expense² was $549 million, up 6%
Loans and Credit Quality | • | Loans and leases were $62.5 billion, up 4%
• | The annualized ratio of net loan and lease charge-offs to average loans and leases was 0.02%, compared with 0.37%
• | The provision for credit losses was a benefit of $8 million, compared with an expense of $49 million
• | Nonperforming assets were $315 million, or 0.50% of loans and leases and other real estate owned, compared with $324 million, or 0.54%
• | Classified loans were $2.1 billion, or 3.40% of loans and leases, compared with $2.4 billion, or 4.00%
Deposits and Borrowed Funds | • | Total deposits were $77.9 billion, up 4%; customer deposits (excluding brokered deposits) were $74.5 billion, up 5%
• | Brokered deposits were $3.5 billion, down 9%; short-term borrowings were $843 million, down 76%
• | Long-term debt was $2.4 billion, up 64%, due to senior note issuances over the past year
Capital | • | The estimated CET1 capital ratio was 11.8%, compared with 11.3%
• | Tangible book value per common share was $43.50, up 13%
Notable Items | • | Acquisition of Basis Multifamily Finance agency lending platform completed in July 2026
• | Net credit valuation adjustment (“CVA”) gain on client-related interest rate swaps of $10 million, or $0.05 per share

Harris H. Simmons, Chairman and CEO of Zions Bancorporation, commented, “Third quarter earnings per share increased 20% to $1.78, up from $1.48 a year ago. The higher earnings were primarily a reflection of improved credit quality, as net loan charge-offs were $3 million, down from $56 million a year ago. Although an increased pace of loan payoffs, combined with a highly competitive market, produced flat loan growth compared to the second quarter, customer deposits grew nearly 10% annualized from second quarter levels.” Mr. Simmons continued, “Short- and medium-term interest rates began to rise in the last month of the quarter, and we expect that our moderately asset-sensitive balance sheet should produce stronger net interest income in a higher rate environment, while we're seeing continued improvement in noninterest income that we expect will continue into next year.” Mr. Simmons concluded, “We were pleased to complete the acquisition of Basis Multifamily Finance I, LLC, a subsidiary of Basis Investment Group, at the end of July. This multifamily finance platform becomes an important strategic advantage in serving our commercial real estate clients, particularly in the fast-growing western markets we serve.”
